title: Long-context anchor signatures: cataloging and stable-release for KV retention
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Summary: Establish a reproducible workflow to produce 'anchor signatures' (stable performance fingerprints) per model-variant and per sequence-distribution bucket, publish those signatures into the model catalog, and provide an automated release that pins an anchor version for production KV retention policies. Motivation: Current KV eviction/pinning behavior is reactive and often misaligned with long-tail sequence shapes. By producing signed, versioned signatures for representative sequence clusters and publishing them as canonical artifacts, routing and retention decisions can be deterministic and safely rolled out across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Goals: 1) Define a compact anchor signature format that captures: quantiles of sequence length, KV hit-rate vs prefix length, tail latency percentiles, and memory footprint at checkpoint. 2) Build a pipeline to run controlled long-context microbenchmarks across model variants (fp16/int8/quantized) and output a signature. 3) Add a model-catalog endpoint + metadata fields to store signatures and anchor-version. 4) Implement a runtime flow that can pin eviction/retention policies to a specified anchor-version and fall back to a default policy when unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Anchor signature schema documented and approved in design doc
Automated benchmark pipeline produces deterministic signatures for test models within 5% variance across 5 runs
Model catalog accepts and serves anchor signatures for at least three model families
Runtime honors anchor-version pin for KV retention and exposes a per-request header indicating which anchor-version was used
Console shows a signature comparison view and rollout controls for anchor-version changes
E2E tests exercise fallback behavior when a pinned anchor-version is missing
implementation_plan: Design doc: propose signature schema, serialization format (JSON+stable hashing), and validation rules (owner: Alyssa)
Bench harness: extend longseq-bench to support sequence clustering buckets, produce per-bucket metrics and assemble anchor signature (owner: Rafael)
Catalog API: add /models/{id}/anchors endpoint, store anchor metadata and release notes (owner: Platform API team)
Runtime change: accept anchor-version in model config and use it to select retention/eviction tunables at load-time; implement header X-Anchor-Version for telemetry (owner: Serving Runtime)
Console: add Anchor Manager UI to view signatures and start rollouts (owner: Console UX)
CI: add reproducibility checks and a gate that fails if signature variance across runs exceeds threshold
rollout_steps: Stage 1: Internal testing on canary infra with 2 low-traffic tenants; validate KV hit-rate improvements and no latency regressions
Stage 2: Publish anchors for gold models in model-catalog and enable automatic anchor pin for non-critical tenants for 1 week
Stage 3: Enable anchor pinning for beta tenants with monitoring thresholds enforced (error budget check)
Stage 4: Gradual 25%->50%->100% rollout to production traffic for models with validated signatures
Stage 5: Post-rollout audit and telemetry review, finalize retrofitting plan for Dedicated/Private (on-prem) deployments
test_plan: Unit tests for signature serializer/deserializer and stable-hash computation
Benchmark reproducibility tests: run bench pipeline 5x daily for 3 days and assert metrics within 5%
Integration test: runtime picks correct retention curve for pinned anchor-version across model-variant switch
Chaos test: simulate missing anchor-version in catalog and assert runtime falls back and emits alert
Performance regression test: ensure P95 tail latency does not increase >3% post-pin in standard workload
monitoring: Per-anchor telemetry: kv_hit_rate_by_bucket and tail_latency_by_bucket published to Console
Dashboard: Anchor rollout health with error budget, tail-latency diffs, and KV memory deltas
Alerts: High delta in tail-latency (>5%) or kv_hit_rate drop (>10%) after rollout
Audit log: store anchor-version changes and who triggered rollout for compliance
notes: Signature format should remain compact to avoid inflating catalog storage; consider gzipped JSON blobs and a stable 8-byte hash for identity
Edge cases: very small models with low KV utility should have 'no-anchor' explicit state
For Private deployments, provide an offline bundle (signature + provenance) that customers can import
We must coordinate with Model Onboarding team to surface training provenance and quantization flags in anchor metadata
Consider exposing 'signature drift' alerts when production traffic distribution diverges from the anchored sequence clusters
